title: Hosted API intake sentinel workflow and decision guides for chat/streaming/toolcalls
creator: Maya R. Sinha
description: Background: Increasing enterprise inbound requests to the Hosted API for multi-action chat flows (streaming + tool/function calls + structured outputs) have created friction: long vetting cycles, inconsistent prioritization, and ad-hoc fallbacks. This ticket defines a lightweight, prescriptive intake 'sentinel' workflow that automates early eligibility checks and produces a human-readable decision guide for PMs/SEs to accelerate gating and routing.
proposal: Introduce a four-layer sentinel: 1) signal normalization (parse requested capabilities: streaming, tool-calls, structured schema), 2) automated eligibility checks (SLA tier, data residency, compliance flags), 3) priority scoring (customer revenue, production risk, technical complexity), 4) deterministic routing (self-serve, expedited review, sales-assisted intake). The sentinel emits a triage envelope containing recommended lane, required attachments, suggested rollout guardrails, and fallback model/route suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated to capture explicit signals for streaming, tool/function calls, and desired structured output schemas.
Automated eligibility checks implemented as rule set with test coverage and mock data (edge cases included).
Priority scoring prototype returns stable buckets (low/medium/high) for a seeded set of 100 historical requests with >= 85% agreement with PM panel labels.
Routing decisions produce a recommended lane and a minimum required artifact list (design doc, security checklist, prod-readiness checklist).
Console view shows triage envelope and allows PM to override with reason; change recorded in audit log.
Playbook document published with runbook steps for expedited review and escalation matrix.
tradeoffs: Conservative rules reduce false-positives but may increase manual reviews — tradeoff accepted for first 3 months to avoid accidental enterprise exposure.
Priority scoring combines quantitative signals (usage, revenue) and qualitative tags (regulatory). This hybrid approach adds explainability but requires periodic calibration.
Automating gating for structured outputs risks blocking experimental use cases; we will expose an appeals channel for dev previews.
Embedding the sentinel in the initial self-serve flow increases friction for low-value requests; we will add an opt-out for OSS/academic use with rate limits.
tasks: Finalize signal schema for intake form (fields + enumerations).
Implement eligibility rules engine (feature flagged behind 'sentinel-v1').
Train and validate simple priority scorer using labeled historical intake data.
Design console triage envelope UI and auditing surface (Design: mockups + accessibility review).
Integrate routing actions with existing Hosted API queue classifier and SLA lanes.
Draft and publish triage playbook, escalation matrix, and decision examples (PM-led).
Run a 2-week pilot with 10 enterprise customers and 3 SEs; collect feedback and refine rules.

2025-11-28: Engineering spike completed; prototype rules engine handles 12 rule predicates (Julian).
2025-12-01: Security pre-review flagged KMS requirement for enterprise attachments; added to dependencies (Ravi).
2025-12-02: PM panel annotated 50 seed requests for scoring dataset; observed 88% preliminary agreement (Sofia).
follow_up: Schedule security review for attachments handling and KMS integration before pilot rollout.
Create metrics dashboard for: time-to-decision, manual override rate, and routing accuracy.
Define SLOs for sentinel latency in the intake path (target <= 300ms for automated checks).
notes: We intentionally keep the initial ruleset conservative to prioritize customer safety.
Pilot cohort should include at least one regulated customer (finance/health) to validate compliance signal handling.
Consider making the priority scorer a service later (separate ENG ticket) if we need to scale frequent recalibration.
